bibliographic.title: Reliable, Adaptable, and Attributable Language Models with Retrieval
bibliographic.authors: Akari Asai; Zexuan Zhong; Danqi Chen; Pang Wei Koh; Luke Zettlemoyer; Hannaneh Hajishirzi; Wen-tau Yih
bibliographic.citation_apa: Asai, A., Zhong, Z., Chen, D., Koh, P. W., Zettlemoyer, L., Hajishirzi, H., & Yih, W. (2023). Reliable, adaptable, and attributable language models with retrieval [Preprint].

methodology.method_family: position paper with narrative review of prior empirical literature and roadmap proposal
methodology.study_design: conceptual position paper advocating retrieval-augmented LMs over parametric LMs, reviewing prior findings and outlining a development roadmap
methodology.technology_context: retrieval-augmented language models (RAG), parametric large language models (GPT-4, GPT-3, ChatGPT), datastores, retrievers, NLP applications including question answering and machine translation

eligibility.decision_rationale: Position paper focused on retrieval-augmented LMs for reliability, adaptability, and attribution rather than conversational governance, human oversight, compliance, or regulated-domain deployment. Relevant as foundational technical context for RAG and attributable outputs, but does not directly address governança conversacional in high-stakes regulated environments.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python triage scored borderline_manual (60.67/100, grade C); paper overlaps on RAG/LLM/attribution but lacks governance, accountability, and regulated-context evidence.

appraisal.notes: Clear position-paper objective and structured roadmap, but no primary empirical study, no systematic review protocol, and no regulated or conversational governance context described in provided text.

cerqual.explanation: Internally coherent conceptual argument with cited prior work, but limited adequacy and relevance for a review on conversational governance in regulated LLM systems because the text addresses RAG architecture and LM weaknesses, not oversight, compliance, or sector-specific governance.

coding.subtheme: Reliability, adaptability, and attribution via retrieval
rq_alignment: partial alignment with knowledge/technical grounding and attribution mechanisms; no direct alignment with conversational governance, human oversight, audit, or regulated compliance

synthesis.main_claim: Retrieval-augmented LMs should replace parametric LMs as the next generation of language models because incorporating large-scale datastores at inference can make models more reliable, adaptable, and attributable.
synthesis.contribution: Advocates a roadmap for general-purpose retrieval-augmented LMs covering datastore/retriever redesign, improved retriever-LM interaction pipelines, and infrastructure investment; synthesizes prior evidence that RAG reduces factual errors, improves attribution, and supports adaptivity and data opt-out.
synthesis.limitations: Current retrieval-augmented LMs struggle beyond knowledge-intensive tasks, have limited retriever-LM interaction, and lack scaling infrastructure; merely scaling parametric models has been insufficient to overcome fundamental weaknesses.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for RAG as a technical mechanism supporting reliability and attribution in LLM systems; not suitable as central evidence for conversational governance, human oversight, compliance, or regulated-domain deployment.
